scenarios.name: single filer, Bailey-vested NC state government pension (stipulated: 5+ years creditable service as of 8/12/1989): fully exempt under the Bailey settlement, engine taxes it in full
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits': 'the North Carolina Consolidated Judicial Retirement System, the Federal Employees' Retirement System, or the United States Civil Service Retirement System, if the retiree had five or more years of creditable service as of August 12, 1989' are exempt from NC income tax; a retiree entitled to the exclusion claims a deduction on 'Line 20, Form D-400, Schedule S 2025 Supplemental Schedule'. This fixture STIPULATES in prose (not in any structured field -- the model has no vesting-date field at all: a household with two government pensions of the identical PlanSource where only one is Bailey-vested cannot be expressed, because both rows decode to the same planSource with no way to distinguish them) that this taxpayer had 5+ years of creditable service in the NC state retirement system as of 8/12/1989, i.e. is Bailey-vested. Arithmetic: $50,000 fully excluded, $0 state taxable income after the $12,750 single standard deduction, tax = $0.00.

knownDefect.summary: Bailey-vested NC state/local/federal government pensions are fully exempt from NC tax; statetax-2026-NC.json has no perSourceExemptions (and the model has no vesting-date field to express Bailey status at all -- a household with two government pensions of the identical PlanSource where only one is Bailey-vested cannot be expressed, because both rows decode to the same planSource with no way to distinguish them), so the engine taxes it in full.

scenarios.name: single filer, private-sector pension (never Bailey-eligible): correctly fully taxable, engine also taxes it fully -- contrast/regression case
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits': the exclusion is scoped to specific NC/federal government retirement systems and 'does not apply to retirement benefits paid to former teachers and state employees of OTHER states'; a private-sector employer pension is never a Bailey-covered retirement system regardless of vesting date, so it remains fully taxable under general NC law. Arithmetic: $50,000 - $12,750 single standard deduction = $37,250 taxable x 3.99% flat rate = $1,486.27 (computed as an IEEE-754 double, matching the engine's own arithmetic to the cent).

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses Bailey-vested NC state pensions (stipulated): fully exempt, engine taxes the full household income
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits' (see single-filer case above for the exact quote). No dollar cap is stated -- 'All distributions from a qualifying Bailey retirement account...are exempt from state income tax regardless of the source of the funds contained in the account.' This fixture stipulates both spouses are Bailey-vested. Arithmetic: $40,000 + $35,000 = $75,000, all fully excluded, $0 taxable after the $25,500 MFJ standard deduction, tax = $0.00.

knownDefect.summary: Both spouses' Bailey-vested pensions should be fully excluded; the engine has no perSourceExemptions for NC, taxing the full $75,000 household income.

scenarios.name: MFJ, one spouse's Bailey-vested NC pension is exempt and the other spouse's private pension is not: one spouse qualifies
scenarios.source: NCDOR 'Bailey Decision Concerning Federal, State and Local Retirement Benefits'. Arithmetic: $40,000 Bailey-vested pension fully excluded; $35,000 private pension fully taxable. $75,000 - $25,500 MFJ standard deduction - $40,000 exclusion = $9,500 taxable x 3.99% = $379.05.

knownDefect.summary: The Bailey-vested spouse's pension should be excluded while the private-pension spouse's income stays taxable; the engine excludes neither (no perSourceExemptions for NC), taxing the full $75,000 -- the identical figure the fully-exempt MFJ case above produces.
